packageRules.description: The minor, patch and digest updates, but Firefox's (below), go into ONE weekly PR: one build of each image per week instead of one per dependency, and no rebase-and-rebuild cascade when one of many PRs merges. A major gets a PR of its own, the Fedora release one for all of its pins (below); every one of them merges itself once ci-ok is green, as everything here does but a moved tag

cosign and its installer (cosign-release, sigstore/cosign-installer: the sign action's and ci.yml's pins job's) wait for the owner, in a PR of their own: a pull request cannot run the sign job, which holds the key, so a new cosign signs for the first time on main, after the moving tags moved (its defaults have changed under this invocation before: .github/actions/sign). Out of the weekly group, which one update that does not merge itself would hold whole. Before the moved-tag rule below, which still takes a moved tag of the installer. tools.txt's cosign, a development tool, is not this

Updates wait 3 days after their release, so a broken or pulled release is usually gone before it is merged. Only for datasources that report release times (endoflife.date gives a Fedora release's date, Docker Hub when a tag was pushed): without one Renovate would hold the update forever (minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour timestamp-required). Not Firefox's (a security release, at once)

Every action is pinned to a commit for an exact version tag, so a digest update of one means that tag was moved to a different commit, which is what a hijacked action looks like (tj-actions/changed-files, 2025). Never automerged, never mixed into the weekly PR (one non-automerge update would hold the whole group), opened at once

A digest update of an unchanged version means that what the version names was replaced upstream, as with a moved GitHub action tag: a release built from its git tag, pinned to the tag's commit as well (a _COMMIT beside the version: REMMINA_COMMIT in apps/org.remmina.Remmina/Containerfile, a GitLab tag; ZYPAK_COMMIT in apps/io.github.lucarickli.Code/Containerfile, a GitHub tag), or an image pinned to its tag's digest as well (the builder's BuildKit in build/build.sh). A new release moves both in one update, which automerges. Never automerged, never in the weekly PR, opened at once. Not a release file pinned by its sha256 (sha256:<hex> in tools/tools.txt and tools/extensions.txt, the github-release-attachments datasource): a new release moves version and sha256 together, but Renovate never reports a file replaced at the same version (it looks up a new digest only for a new version); install.sh catches that when the Monday builds download it again, and notify.yml opens the issue. The custom managers only: an action's tag is a github-tags dependency too, and has its own group above

zypak (ZYPAK_VERSION in apps/io.github.lucarickli.Code/Containerfile): its releases only, the tags Flathub's Electron BaseApp follows (its x-checker's tag-pattern ^v([\d.]+)$, branch/26.08), not its betas (v2020.10beta.1)

Claude Code (CLAUDE_VERSION in apps/io.github.lucarickli.Code/Containerfile and devcontainer/Containerfile) follows Anthropic's stable channel, the npm dist-tag 'stable': a release about a week old, skipping those with major regressions, instead of every daily one

The Fedora base images are not managed as docker tags: the registry carries the next release (branched) and rawhide as plain numbers long before they are released, so a docker lookup would propose rawhide. The fedora custom manager below follows released Fedora versions instead

COPY --from=tools and --from=keys in the Containerfiles name the build contexts build/docker-bake.hcl passes (tools/ and keys/), and FROM runtime and FROM sdk the runtime's and the SDK's image it passes (the named contexts runtime and sdk), not images of a registry: the dockerfile manager would look them up on Docker Hub

Firefox (FIREFOX_VERSION in apps/org.mozilla.firefox/Containerfile) follows Mozilla's current release, the one version product-details.mozilla.org names (customDatasources.firefox): N.0, then its dot releases N.0.x, in loose versioning. A browser release is a security update, so every one, each new N (a major) too, gets a PR of its own at any time, not on the weekend schedule, in a group of its own instead of the weekly one, and automerges once ci-ok is green

The move to the next Fedora release: every pin in one PR, opened 3 days after endoflife.date gives its release date (not on the weekend after), which merges itself once ci-ok is green, as a major does: the dev container, the runtime, the SDK and every app on them build and test on it first

customManagers.description: The Fedora release, in one PR: the dev container's (the fedora-toolbox tag in devcontainer/Containerfile), the scanner container's (scan.sh) and the builder's (build/Containerfile), and the runtime's, which is its branch and the SDK's: the FROM line of runtime/Containerfile, the flatpak.branch of the runtime and of the SDK (runtime/sdk/Containerfile), io.github.lucarickli.Platform//N in the flatpak.runtime of the runtime's test stage and of every app on it (apps/*/Containerfile), and io.github.lucarickli.Sdk//N in the SDK's test stage and the VS Code Flatpak's

Tool versions in the workflows and the composite actions under a '# renovate: datasource=... depName=...' comment (zizmor, Renovate, minisign, slsa-verifier in ci.yml); an action's cosign-release, and the buildx release setup-buildx-action installs (its version, in .github/actions/buildx), are the github-actions manager's

The development tools and VS Code extensions in tools/tools.txt and tools/extensions.txt: the line under each '# renovate:' comment is 'name version asset checksum members license [source]'. A checksum of sha256:<hex> (releases that publish none) is the digest the github-release-attachments datasource bumps with the version; the #sha256:<hex> of a license URL is not matched and stays as it is
The BuildKit of the builder every image is baked on (build/build.sh), under a '# renovate: datasource=docker depName=...' comment: its tag, and that tag's digest, which moves with it

Versions under a renovate comment in the Containerfiles (ARG lines); a tag's commit after the version, on the same line (NAME_COMMIT=<40 hex>, as REMMINA_COMMIT and ZYPAK_COMMIT), is its digest, which moves with it
